name: Denver

electric.name: Xcel Energy (Colorado)
electric.serves: Electric service for Denver and much of the metro. Denver's homeowner pages send residents to Xcel rebates, and Xcel's Home Energy Squad page refers to 'the Denver metro area'.

gas.name: Xcel Energy (Colorado natural gas)
gas.serves: Natural gas for Denver and much of the metro. Xcel's Colorado gas furnace rebates require being a 'Colorado Xcel Energy residential natural gas customer'.

utilities.notes: Xcel's Colorado rebate rules turn on fuel. Bonuses go to Xcel natural-gas customers. Since November 16, 2025, homes with existing electric heat get standard heat pump rebates only, with no bonus. Xcel gas-only customers whose electricity comes from another utility get no Xcel heat pump rebate. Electric cooperatives and municipal utilities serve some outer parts of the metro; they were not checked individually.

auditPrograms.name: Xcel Energy Home Energy Squad (Colorado): Squad, Squad Plus and Virtual visits
auditPrograms.cost: The standard Squad visit is listed at '$50 FREE for a limited time'. Squad Plus, which includes a full energy audit, is '$150 Now only $100, for a limited time' with Xcel's audit rebate already taken off. The virtual visit is $0.
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: Residential Xcel Energy customers in Colorado whose home has its own utility account and is a detached single-family home or in a building of four or fewer units. Renters need the owner's prior approval.
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: The Squad visit includes free install of LEDs, weather-stripping for an exterior door, efficient showerheads and aerators, a smart thermostat with AC Rewards enrollment, and a water heater temperature check (Xcel calls it 'a $200 value'). Squad Plus adds an inspection of the exterior, insulation and mechanical systems, a blower-door air-leak test, a combustion safety test, a carbon monoxide check, infrared imaging, a full report and free advising ('a $600 value'). The virtual visit is a video walk-through with a free DIY kit.
auditPrograms.howToBook: Online at xcelenergycores.clearesult.com. Allow up to 10 days to schedule.
auditPrograms.status: Open as of 2026-10-12. The $50-free and $100 Squad Plus prices are 'for a limited time' with no end date given.

auditPrograms.name: Xcel Energy Home Energy Audit rebate (independent registered auditors)
auditPrograms.cost: You pay the auditor up front, then Xcel rebates 60% of the audit price: up to $100 for a Standard Audit, $160 with a blower door, and $200 with infrared.
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: Colorado Xcel residential electric and/or gas customers in single-family homes up to a four-plex, once every two years, using a registered audit contractor. The Infrared audit needs Xcel gas service, or Xcel electric service with electric space heating.
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: Standard: exterior, windows and doors, insulation, mechanical systems, a CO test and a bill analysis. Blower Door adds air-leakage testing and combustion safety testing. Infrared adds thermal imaging. After the audit, CLEAResult Energy Advisors give free follow-up (303.446.7910).
auditPrograms.howToBook: Choose a registered auditor from Xcel's participating contractor search (hvacree.net/xcel-co). Questions: 800-895-4999.
auditPrograms.status: Open. Listed in Xcel's 2026 Colorado Rebate Summary (effective October 1, 2026).

auditPrograms.name: Xcel Energy Income-Qualified Home Energy Squad (Colorado)
auditPrograms.whoQualifies: Colorado Xcel electric and/or gas customers who receive Xcel bill assistance, are in LEAP, SNAP, TANF or weatherization, meet state income guidelines, or live in a disproportionately impacted community. Renters need landlord approval.
auditPrograms.whatYouGet: A full assessment (blower door, combustion safety, CO check, infrared, report) with on-the-spot installs (LEDs, weather-stripping, showerheads and aerators, thermostat). Follow-up rebates can cover up to 100% of air sealing, insulation (wall, crawl space, attic, storm windows), heat pumps, heat pump water heaters or evaporative coolers.

rebates.name: Xcel Energy heat pump rebates (Colorado, 2026 Rebate Summary effective Oct. 1, 2026)
rebates.amount: Standard rebate, with the standard-plus-bonus figure in brackets. Ducted or mixed-ducted air-source heat pump: $300 per cooling ton [$600]. Ducted cold-climate heat pump: $750 per heating ton at 5°F [$1,500]. Ground-source: $1,100 per heating ton [$2,200]. Air-to-water: $950 per heating ton [$1,900]. Non-ducted heat pumps heating at least 50% of the home: the same per-ton amounts as ducted. Supplemental mini-splits (garage, room, or not reducing gas use): $500, with no bonus.
rebates.whoQualifies: Colorado Xcel residential customers. A Trade Partner Network contractor is required except for supplemental mini-splits. Bonuses need a 2026-dated invoice and are not available to homes whose existing primary heat is electric (effective November 16, 2025). Xcel gas-only customers with electricity from another provider don't qualify. Rebates can't exceed project cost.
rebates.status: Open. 'Invoices and installations must be completed by Dec. 31, 2026, but applications for rebates will be accepted through Sept. 30, 2027.' Funding is first come, first served.

rebates.name: Xcel Energy heat pump water heater rebate (Colorado)
rebates.amount: $750 standard, or $1,500 with the bonus (ENERGY STAR, 3.3 UEF)
rebates.whoQualifies: Colorado Xcel customers. The bonus rules match the heat pump rebate: a 2026 invoice, and no bonus for homes with existing electric heat.

rebates.name: Xcel Energy insulation and air sealing rebates (Colorado)
rebates.amount: For customers heating with Xcel electricity or gas: air sealing 30% of cost up to $400 (at least a 20% CFM50 reduction); wall insulation 30% up to $350 (empty cavity to R-13 or more); attic insulation 30% up to $500 (from below R-24 to R-60 or more, per the Oct. 1, 2026 summary). Xcel gas-heat customers get a bonus of 1.5 times the standard rebate with a 2026 invoice. Cooling-only Xcel electric customers get $15, $25 or $60. A $600 bonus applies when the insulation and air sealing and a qualifying heat pump are installed within two years of each other.
rebates.whoQualifies: Existing homes up to four units. Work must be done by a BPI-certified participating contractor. Mobile homes, new construction and additions are excluded.
rebates.status: Open. Applications are due by July 31 of the year after the work. Xcel's insulation web page still shows older thresholds (pre-job under R-15, post-job R-49) and a '2025' bonus footnote, which conflicts with the summary dated effective Oct. 1, 2026.

rebates.name: Xcel Energy Whole Home Efficiency bonus (Colorado)
rebates.amount: A 25% bonus on all standard rebates, plus larger attic insulation and washer/dryer rebates, when three or more measures are installed within two years of enrolling
rebates.whoQualifies: Customers with Xcel natural gas service, or Xcel electric service with electric heating
rebates.status: Listed in the 2026 Colorado Rebate Summary

rebates.name: Xcel Energy gas furnace and boiler rebates (Colorado), ending
rebates.amount: Gas furnace at 95%+ AFUE: $225. Boiler at 95%+: $225. Boiler with side-arm water heater: $325. Each must replace non-condensing equipment.
rebates.whoQualifies: Colorado Xcel residential natural gas customers
rebates.status: Ending. 'Effective Jan. 1, 2027, gas furnace and boiler rebates will be removed from Xcel Energy's offerings.' Equipment invoiced in 2026 can be submitted through September 30, 2027.

rebates.name: Colorado Heat Pump Tax Credit (contractor-delivered discount)
rebates.runBy: Colorado Energy Office and Colorado Department of Revenue
rebates.amount: For installs on or after January 1, 2026: air-source heat pump credit $1,000, with at least $333 discounted to the customer. Ground-, water- or combined-source credit $2,000, with at least $667 to the customer. Heat pump water heater credit $250, with at least $83 to the customer. The 2024-2025 amounts ($1,500, $3,000 and $500) have expired.
rebates.whoQualifies: Anyone installing an eligible ENERGY STAR heat pump in Colorado through a registered contractor. The contractor claims the credit and must show a 'State of Colorado Heat Pump Discount' on the invoice; customers file nothing.
rebates.status: Active for 2026 installs. Contractors can register for 2026 installs until December 31, 2026. Credit amounts drop again in tax year 2029.

rebates.name: Power Ahead Colorado heat pump rebate (DRCOG)
rebates.runBy: Denver Regional Council of Governments (Power Ahead Colorado)
rebates.amount: 'Save $1500 when you upgrade to an energy-efficient heat pump.' The initial phase covers cold-climate air-source heat pumps in existing buildings.
rebates.whoQualifies: Single-family, multifamily and commercial retrofits in DRCOG-participating municipalities and counties. An approved contractor must get preapproval before work starts. It can be combined with utility and local rebates.
rebates.status: Described as in its 'initial phase'. The page gives no open, closed or funds-remaining status. Energy Advisors: 844-303-9333.

rebates.name: Denver Solar and Heat Pump Group Buy (Switch Together Denver)
rebates.runBy: City and County of Denver (Office of Climate Action, Sustainability and Resiliency) with Switch Together
rebates.amount: A group-buying discount: 'Participants can save up to 10% compared to the average cost of installation'. It stacks with Xcel, Colorado Energy Office and Power Ahead Colorado rebates.
rebates.whoQualifies: Denver homeowners. Sign up, complete an intake form and get a vetted installer's quote, with no obligation.
rebates.status: Active as of 2026-10-12. The City says Switch Together mailers 'were sent in April, May, and July 2026'.

rebates.name: Colorado RENU loan (Colorado Clean Energy Fund)
rebates.runBy: Colorado Clean Energy Fund with Colorado credit unions
rebates.amount: Up to $75,000 for up to 20 years at a fixed rate, with no money down and no prepayment penalty. It is secured by a UCC-1 on the installed equipment, with no lien on the property.
rebates.whoQualifies: Owners of existing Colorado single-family homes (primary, secondary or rental), plus townhomes and condos without shared heating or cooling systems

stateHomeEnergyRebates.status: closed for single-family homes (as of 2026-10-12). HEAR Region 1 (Front Range, including the Denver metro) and Region 2 both show '$0 remaining' and 'Program Closed' on the dashboard last updated 2026-08-03. HEAR for small multifamily and HER (HOMES) for manufactured homes and large multifamily are slated for 2026 and not yet open.
stateHomeEnergyRebates.programName: Colorado Home Energy Rebate Program: Home Electrification and Appliance Rebates (HEAR) and Home Efficiency Rebates (HER)
stateHomeEnergyRebates.administrator: Colorado Energy Office (help center run by Guidehouse: 866-336-0016, COenergyrebates@guidehouse.com)
stateHomeEnergyRebates.summary: The single-family HEAR program has launched and is now closed statewide. CEO says: 'The HEAR Single-Family Program for Region 1 and Region 2 is closed' (updated August 2026). Region 1, the Front Range, includes Adams, Arapahoe, Broomfield, Clear Creek, Denver, Douglas, Elbert and Jefferson counties. CEO's HEAR dashboard (last updated 08/3/26) shows '$0 remaining' and 'Program Closed' for both regions. About $45.6 million was available: $31.9 million for single-family households and $13.7 million for multifamily buildings under 50,000 sq ft. The small-multifamily HEAR rebates and the HER (HOMES) rebates for manufactured/mobile homes and large multifamily buildings are slated for 2026 but not yet open to single-family homes. The HEAR terms, for reference: below 80% AMI, 100% of qualified cost; 80-150% AMI, 50%. Caps were $8,000 for a cold-climate heat pump, $3,000 for other heat pumps, $1,750 for a heat pump water heater, $4,000 for a panel, $2,500 for wiring, $1,600 for insulation, air sealing and ventilation, and $840 for an electric stove, with a $14,000 total.

incomeQualified.name: Colorado Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP)
incomeQualified.runBy: Colorado Energy Office through local providers. Denver, Jefferson, Broomfield and Gilpin: Energy Resource Center, Denver Metro Regional Office, (720) 236-1321. Adams and Arapahoe: Arapahoe County Weatherization Division, (303) 636-1982. Douglas and Elbert: Energy Resource Center, Pikes Peak Regional Office, (719) 591-0772. Clear Creek and Park: Northwest Colorado Council of Governments, 1-800-332-3669. Buildings with 5+ units: Energy Outreach Colorado, (303) 825-8750.
incomeQualified.summary: No-cost weatherization for income-qualified homeowners and renters, including manufactured homes. A free home energy audit is required. Services can include air sealing, attic, floor and wall insulation, furnace repair or replacement, LEDs, efficient appliances, and air-source heat pumps 'on a limited basis'. Income limits vary by county; households on AND, TANF, SSI, SNAP or LEAP may qualify automatically. CEO warns 'Eligible households may be placed on a waiting list.' Homes weatherized in the past 15 years are ineligible. Apply online or through your local provider.

incomeQualified.name: Xcel Energy Income-Qualified Home Energy Squad and upgrades
incomeQualified.summary: A free diagnostic visit with on-the-spot installs, then up to 100% coverage of air sealing, insulation, heat pumps, heat pump water heaters or evaporative coolers for eligible customers. Eligibility comes through bill assistance, LEAP, SNAP or TANF enrollment, state income guidelines, or living in a disproportionately impacted community.

incomeQualified.name: Denver Cool Homes Mini-Grants and LEAP referral
incomeQualified.summary: 'Up to $50,000 is available for community-based organizations and nonprofits to install portable AC units' for residents most vulnerable to extreme heat. Homeowners can't apply directly. Denver's heat-resources page also points residents to Colorado's Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) for bill help.

localRules.name: Energize Denver Building Performance Policy
localRules.appliesTo: Commercial and multifamily buildings of 5,000 sq ft or more only. Single-family homeowners are not affected.
localRules.summary: Large buildings (25,000 sq ft and up) must meet energy-saving goals, and small buildings (5,000-24,999 sq ft) must complete certain upgrades. Denver states the policy is 'not a requirement to electrify heating or cooling systems' and 'not a mandate to replace HVAC equipment before the end of its useful life'.

localRules.name: Building Performance Colorado (state benchmarking and BPS)
localRules.appliesTo: Most commercial buildings of 50,000 sq ft or more. Ordinary homeowners are not affected.
localRules.summary: Covered buildings benchmark every year (reporting opens July 1, report and fee due November 1; the 2026 period is open now) and must meet building performance standards aimed at cutting commercial building emissions 7% by 2026 and 20% by 2030, compared with 2021.

localRules.name: Denver Energy Code: existing residential buildings
localRules.appliesTo: Homeowners doing permitted additions, alterations or renovations in Denver
localRules.summary: 'Existing residential buildings undergoing an addition, alteration, and/or renovation or use must follow the appropriate sections of the Denver Energy Code.' The 2025 Denver Energy Code has residential amendments. The specific electrification or equipment-replacement requirements for existing homes were not checked here.

notes: As of 2026-10-12: (1) Colorado's IRA HEAR rebates for single-family homes are closed in the Denver metro ($0 remaining since the August 2026 dashboard). (2) Xcel's 2026 Colorado Rebate Summary took effect October 1, 2026. Gas furnace and boiler rebates end January 1, 2027, heat pump bonuses require 2026 invoices, and homes already on electric heat get no bonus. (3) The state heat pump tax credit dropped for 2026 (air-source $1,000 credit, $333 minimum customer discount). (4) Denver's homeowner incentives now point to a Switch Together group buy plus Xcel, Colorado Energy Office and Power Ahead Colorado rebates. Denver's current CASR pages show no open City-funded residential 'Climate Action Rebate' for heat pumps; the building rebates listed (ASHRAE Level 2 audit rebates, showcase grants, an Energize Denver compliance gap fund) target commercial and multifamily buildings. If Denver reopens homeowner Climate Action Rebates, a new page will be needed; none was linked from the City's pages on 2026-10-12. Xcel's Colorado rebate amounts come from the official 2026 Rebate Summary PDF linked from Xcel's heat pump page. Federal 25C/25D credits ended for property placed in service after 2025 (IRS).
